profile_name: WTF Mystery / Unknown Causes and Progressive Answers
mission: Find mysteries where something is WRONG, UNKNOWN or IMPOSSIBLE and the story keeps working out what is happening, why, what the rules are and what the actual explanation is. Unexplained phenomena, hidden causes, reality and time puzzles, trapped worlds, hidden organisations and twisty culprit hunts all qualify. This profile exists because a premise is not a mystery: a story can open with a magnificent unanswered question and then spend its runtime on relationship, grief or faction drama, or simply stop delivering, and that is the concrete disappointment it is built to avoid. So central_mystery and mystery_density are measured separately, investigation is measured separately from revelation cadence, and one enormous final twist is measured separately from a story that keeps rebuilding what you understood. Under the Dome, Dark, Lost, Severance, Archive 81 and Bodies are the shape being sought; The Rain and The Mist are cited as further descriptions of that shape only, with no viewing implied and, for The Mist, no adaptation identity assumed. Supernatural and impossible causes are welcome when they serve the central question; paranormal horror delivered for scares with a thin mystery attached is not. Natural, biological, environmental and scientific causes are equally welcome. An earlier-era visual presentation is a ranking penalty and never an exclusion, and RELEASE YEAR IS NEVER AN INPUT to it.

automation_rules.past_24h_definition: Only items with added_by=daily-automation and added_at within the last 24 hours. Bootstrap items carry added_by=bootstrap and never appear in this row.
automation_rules.match_score_definition: match_score IS the deterministic baseline DNA score: the dna-match row score, post-archetype-bonus, post-guardrail, clamped 0..100. It is COMPUTED by scripts/dna-score.mjs, never an invented holistic judgement and never a felt number. The thresholds are on that same scale and were calibrated against THIS profile's own distribution. They are NOT comparable to Thriller 62/80, Fantasy 65/80, Action 60/70, Anime 58/67 or Sci-Fi 82/90.
automation_rules.calibration_note: CALIBRATED against this profile's own deterministic score distribution over a 95-title pool that deliberately contained every failure shape this addon exists to reject, because a pool of good mysteries would prove nothing about the rules. 20 fell below the DNA row floor or were hard-excluded; 75 scored: min 50, Q1 65, median 76, Q3 84, max 100. EVERY guardrail fired on real pool members, none is untested: premise_without_density on The Leftovers, The Society, Mare of Easttown, Sharp Objects, Mystic River and Personal Shopper; slow_procedural_without_payoff on Broadchurch, The Night Of, The Killing, The Undoing, Sharp Objects and Mystic River; drama_drift on twelve titles including Constellation, The Terror, Bad Sisters and La Brea; paranormal_horror_first on The Others, The Sixth Sense, The Conjuring, Insidious and Grave Encounters; survival_without_question on A Quiet Place and Greenland; low_revelation_mystery on Personal Shopper; romance_drama_dominant on The Time Traveler's Wife; cheap_presentation on Grave Encounters. The single hard exclusion fired on exactly one title, Greenland, whose central_mystery is 2. minimum_match_score is NOT a quartile: it is the empirical separating line between two classes that do not overlap in this pool. The highest-scoring designed negative is Hereditary at 60 and the lowest-scoring title the user positively wants is The Pale Blue Eye at 61, with an eleven-title band from 50 to 60 containing nothing but designed negatives and titles the user rated unappealing. Q1 (65) was rejected because it would cut Zodiac (63), Yellowjackets (63) and The Pale Blue Eye (61), all explicit user interests, which would make the threshold an aesthetic choice rather than a derived one. best_match_score sits at 85, Q3+1, inside the 84-to-86 gap, capturing the top 23% (17 titles). IMPORTANT BOUNDARY CASES: Dept. Q scores 63 and SURVIVES, which is the point - a genuinely twisty procedural is wanted and being a procedural is never the objection, while Broadchurch, The Night Of, The Killing, Mare of Easttown and Sharp Objects all fall below the floor on cadence and drama share. The Outsider (75) and Archive 81 (86) are supernatural and are NOT rejected, while The Others, The Conjuring and Insidious are, which is the paranormal-horror split working. Identity (84) and Memento (78) carry high retro_visual_style and stay high because their mysteries are strong - retro is a linear penalty referenced by NO guardrail, exactly as specified. Knives Out, the user's strongest watched anchor, scores 76 rather than topping the list because it has zero unexplained phenomenon, zero unknown rules and zero temporal anomaly; that is honest and is the clearest evidence this is not a whodunit addon wearing a Mystery label. Wayward Pines is the one real tension: it scores 82 on genuinely strong containment, conspiracy and hidden-truth structure while the user's unwatched impression was only lukewarm, so it is recorded here rather than smoothed away, and it is not bootstrapped. THESE NUMBERS ARE MYSTERY-SPECIFIC and are not comparable to Thriller 62/80, Fantasy 65/80, Action 60/70, Anime 58/67 or Sci-Fi 82/90.

principles.descriptive_only: A DNA value describes how strongly a property exists in a TITLE. It never states whether that property is desirable. supernatural_cause 9 means the impossible explanation is strongly present, NOT that it is liked; retro_visual_style 9 means the presentation strongly reads as an earlier era, NOT that the work is bad. Desirability lives only in dna_baseline and dna_guardrails.
principles.unknown_is_not_zero: Missing or null means UNKNOWN, never 'definitely absent'. Never substitute 0, and never use null to avoid research.
principles.unknown_never_satisfies: A threshold comparison against an unknown value is false in both directions.
principles.unknown_is_not_safe: Unknown must not be read as 'passes the guardrail'. An item is not DNA-score-eligible unless every dimension referenced anywhere in dna_guardrails is known - which for this profile specifically includes mystery_density, revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation, because an unmeasured cadence is exactly how a premise-only show or a silent procedural would slip through.
principles.independent_dimensions: THE SEPARATIONS THIS PROFILE EXISTS FOR. central_mystery is how strong the unresolved question is; mystery_density is how much of the WHOLE RUNTIME actually pushes it - a show can be 9 and 3. investigation is how much inquiry work exists; revelation_frequency is how often meaningful information lands; progressive_revelation is whether it REFRAMES what was understood - a procedural can be 9, 3 and 3. plot_twists is reversals delivered; a film built on one enormous final twist is high there and only moderate on progressive_revelation, because nothing was rebuilt along the way. supernatural_cause is an impossible explanation being present; paranormal_horror_focus is haunting and possession material delivered for scares - Archive 81 and The Outsider are high on the first and moderate on the second, The Others and A Haunting in Venice the reverse. scientific_cause and supernatural_cause are both legitimate answers to the same question and neither is preferred for its kind. visual_quality is craft and retro_visual_style is era aesthetic; they are independent and RELEASE YEAR IS NEVER AN INPUT to either. weirdness is strangeness, which can exist with no mystery at all.

dna_baseline.description: The desired CONTENT universe expressed on the DNA scale. Stable baseline. Accumulated user feedback is NEVER merged into this section.
dna_baseline.scale_note: Weights are -40..40 and commensurate only within this profile. central_mystery and mystery_density sit jointly at the top because the premise and its whole-runtime delivery are equally load-bearing. progressive_revelation and revelation_frequency at 18 sit ABOVE investigation at 12: this profile buys the answers, not the procedure. scientific_cause (8) and supernatural_cause (6) are both positive - the kind of explanation is not the preference, the pursuit of one is. paranormal_horror_focus carries the largest negative because the objection is scare-delivery, not the impossible. A shared dimension id carries no shared weight with any other WTF profile.
dna_baseline.unweighted_note: pace_speed is the sole unweighted dimension. Speed is NOT itself desirable here: Lost was explicitly slow and sometimes boring and was still liked because the island phenomenon kept mattering, while a fast story that reveals nothing is not wanted. So pace carries no linear weight and is used only inside slow_procedural_without_payoff, where slowness is one of four conditions rather than the objection. weights and unweighted are disjoint and their union is exactly the 30 registry ids.

completeness_defaults.note: An item must satisfy ALL THREE conditions to be DNA-score-eligible. required_known_dimensions contains every dimension referenced anywhere in dna_guardrails - critically mystery_density, revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation - plus retro_visual_style, which no guardrail may reference but which must always be measured so the era aesthetic is never silently skipped. NOTE that min_known_dimensions is NOT the binding constraint for the DNA Match row: requiredFor() independently demands every weighted dimension, so a title reaching DNA Match needs all 29 weighted values. Lowering min_known_dimensions would relieve nothing that binds - research fewer titles instead.

dna_baseline.archetype_note: Best-matching archetype only, never an average. EVERY archetype emphasises BOTH mystery_density and revelation_frequency at 7 or more, by construction. Archetypes describe different SHAPES of mystery and must never become the route by which a magnificent premise with no whole-runtime delivery, or a heavy investigation with no payoff, collects a large bonus. impossible_cause_mystery additionally REQUIRES central_mystery and unknown_rules and penalises paranormal_horror_focus, so 'a ghost is present' can never match it.

dna_guardrails.description: Policy applied to descriptive DNA measurements. Not learnable away by ordinary feedback.
dna_guardrails.evaluation_note: A condition whose dimension is unknown/null evaluates FALSE. This profile has exactly ONE hard exclusion - a title with no central mystery at all - and every other negative context is a contextual combination penalty, so a strong enough title can still clear the bar despite one.

hard_exclusion.note: A title with essentially no unresolved central question is not a Mystery recommendation, however good it is otherwise. This is an INGESTION gate, not only a scoring one: the Full Watchlist row does not consult DNA and would publish a title that every ranked row excludes. The bound is deliberately low - anything with a real open question clears it - and it is the ONLY hard exclusion in this profile.

combination.note: THE defining rule of this addon. A huge unexplained premise can be set up in episode one and then effectively abandoned while the runtime goes to interpersonal or faction material, or simply stops delivering. central_mystery measures how strong the question is; mystery_density measures how much of the WHOLE RUNTIME actually pushes it. A great premise is not a great mystery, and an episode-one hook is never evidence of density.

Procedure is not payoff. A detective can investigate for ten hours while almost nothing meaningful lands and nothing is reframed. This fires ONLY when the investigation is present AND the cadence, the reframing and the forward motion are all absent - a twisty procedural is exactly what the profile wants, and being a procedural is never the objection.
Nothing is landing, the mystery is not being worked, and no tension is being sustained. Catches the low-payoff case where there is no formal investigation to trip the rule above.

Haunting, possession and seance material delivered for scares with only a thin mystery attached. THE SUPERNATURAL IS NEVER THE OBJECTION: an impossible cause serving a real central question, with rules and answers arriving, is actively wanted and cannot fire this rule, because it requires the central mystery AND the reframing to both be weak.

The runtime has gone to relationship, family, grief or faction drama and the mystery has become the frame rather than the subject. Drama is measured descriptively and is never disqualifying on its own - a dense mystery with heavy drama does not fire this.

A deadly environment is not a mystery. If people simply run from a known danger for the whole runtime, with no live question about what caused it, how it works or whether the apparent rules are correct, this is not the profile. Under the Dome is the counter-example and cannot fire this: its cause, rules and origin are all open.
A relationship drama wearing mystery clothing. Sustained suspense makes it moot.

CRAFT, NEVER AGE. retro_visual_style is deliberately absent from every guardrail in this profile: an earlier-era look softens ranking through its linear weight alone and must never exclude, because a conceptually exceptional mystery is allowed to overcome it. A high-craft work that simply looks of an earlier era is not cheap.

not_expressible_in_dna.consumer_rule: NO CONSUMER MAY READ, EVALUATE OR SCORE THIS FIELD. It carries zero runtime semantics.

entries.signal: A Mystery genre label on IMDb, TMDB or a streamer
entries.reason: Proves almost nothing. The genre tag says a mystery exists somewhere in the work; it says nothing about whether the mystery is worked across the runtime, whether answers arrive, or whether the runtime actually belongs to drama. Every DNA value must come from researched narrative structure.

entries.signal: Investigation as a proxy for payoff
entries.reason: Explicitly rejected. investigation measures how much inquiry work exists, never whether it pays off. revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation carry the payoff, and slow_procedural_without_payoff exists because conflating them is the failure this profile was built around.

entries.signal: A strong premise as a proxy for mystery density
entries.reason: Explicitly rejected. An unexplained event in episode one is evidence about episode one. Whole-runtime density needs episode guides, recaps and season reviews.

entries.signal: One famous ending twist as a proxy for progressive revelation
entries.reason: Explicitly rejected. plot_twists and progressive_revelation are separate dimensions precisely so a single final reversal cannot masquerade as a story that kept rebuilding what you understood.

entries.signal: Release year / age of the title
entries.reason: Never a preference and never a DNA dimension. The objection is presentation style, measured directly by retro_visual_style, which is weight-only and referenced by NO guardrail. A recent film shot in a period style can be high; a restored older film with a timeless look can be low.

entries.signal: The presence of a supernatural or impossible element
entries.reason: Neither a positive nor a negative in itself. The Outsider and Archive 81 are wanted; The Others and A Haunting in Venice are not. The discriminator is whether the impossible cause serves a central question that keeps being answered, which is why supernatural_cause and paranormal_horror_focus are separate dimensions.

entries.signal: Critical acclaim, awards or IMDb rating
entries.reason: Never taste fit. The Night Of, Mystic River and Memories of Murder are all acclaimed and are all negative anchors here.

execution_preferences.description: Baseline POLICY for how execution evidence would be applied if personalization were enabled. Policy only, and INERT: this repository contains no data/personalized-scores.json.
rules: Personalization is DISABLED for this profile until the cross-profile feedback v3 schema is frozen.
When enabled, a feedback event may be consumed only if its imdb_id is already in THIS repository's own public identity set.
Execution feedback never changes topic or DNA eligibility.
A pacing complaint is execution evidence about one title and never a general preference for faster work - Lost is the standing counter-example.
A single title never establishes a generalised content aversion, and one disliked ghost story never makes supernatural_cause negative.
mystery_density, revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation are NON-PROJECTABLE, so the payoff safeguards can never be learned away.
The stable baseline remains dominant while feedback history is small.

baseline_evidence.description: Audit trail for how the weights above were derived, from a single explicit calibration round of 50 titles. NOT read at runtime: the weights, archetypes and guardrails ARE the encoding of this evidence. SIX public identities are watched-confirmed - Knives Out, The Sixth Sense, Dark, Lost, Severance and Under the Dome - each recording how watching was established, and each therefore permanently excluded from recommendation. Everything else is UNWATCHED and fully recommendable. That deliberately includes The OA, Archive 81, Bodies and Twin Peaks, where there was real partial exposure but no confirmed completion: Stremio carries ONE identity per series, so marking them watched would hide the episodes still unseen. Shutter Island is unwatched because the user explicitly could not remember, and uncertainty resolves to unwatched. Zodiac is unwatched because documentaries about the real case are not the film. The Rain and The Mist appear only in the mission prose as descriptions of the desired shape - no viewing is implied and no adaptation identity is assumed for The Mist. RECOMMENDABLE IS NOT A WANT FLAG. The schema DERIVES it from watched-ness alone - the validator enforces recommendable === (evidence_type === 'unwatched') and rejects any other value - so every unwatched entry here reads true, including the ones the user flatly dismissed. EXPLICIT USER REJECTION THEREFORE LIVES IN data/rejections.json, not in this block, and that file is the authority the daily automation consults. The two are different questions: this block records what the user REACTED to and is the audit trail for the weights; rejections.json records what the user does not want RECOMMENDED. A title can legitimately carry a strong structural DNA score and still be rejected there, and a negative reaction here is NOT by itself a rejection - only a flat dismissal (reaction 'unappealing', no stated positive interest) is, which is why mixed, uncertain and lukewarm entries such as Memento, Twin Peaks, Wayward Pines, True Detective, From, The Leftovers, The Invisible Guest and The Killing stay fully eligible.
